clues: A small, flattened, mononucleated stem cell residing inside the external lamina of an adult muscle fiber.
It remains mitotically quiescent until muscle trauma, ischemia, or heavy exercise activates it.
Activated cells divide into myoblasts that fuse to repair damaged skeletal muscle fibers.
Electron-dense protein plaques scattered in the cytoplasm and along the inner sarcolemma of unstriated muscle.
They contain alpha-actinin and serve as attachment sites for thin actin filaments and desmin intermediate filaments.
They function as the structural equivalent of Z-discs in smooth muscle cells.
